page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel core with hyperthreading. It is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs. The underlying Intel processor features advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES and SHA_NI.

Performance benchmarks indicate moderate single-core capabilities but limited multi-core scaling due to the dual-thread single-core hardware layout. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores rank in the average tier. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the poor and weak categories respectively. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with Passmark memory scores and large-block memory read/write bandwidth benchmarks registering in the bottom 10%.

From a resource density perspective, the n4-highcpu-2 offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, simple text processing, and minor background utility jobs. It is less suitable for memory-intensive database operations, software compilation, or parallelized multi-threaded processing.
